tasks.summary_en: Trapezoid $400,100,h{=}75$: max inscribed rectangle (sum of dimensions and area)
tasks.statement_en: A plot of land has the shape of a trapezoid. The bases $AB$ and $CD$ of this trapezoid have lengths $|AB| = 400$ m and $|CD| = 100$ m. The height of the trapezoid is 75 m, and its angles $DAB$ and $ABC$ are acute. From the plot, a rectangular parking area is to be marked out. Two of the vertices of this rectangle are to lie on base $AB$ of the trapezoid, and the other two - $E$ and $F$ - on legs $AD$ and $BC$ of the trapezoid [Figure: trapezoid ABCD with an inscribed rectangle AEFB shaded, E on AD, F on BC]. Determine the side lengths of the rectangle for which the area of the marked-out lot will be greatest. Determine this greatest area. Show your working. Hint: to relate the rectangle's dimensions, use that the area of trapezoid $ABCD$ equals the sum of the areas of trapezoids $ABFE$ and $EFCD$.
tasks.notes: Value sums all three requested numbers: rectangle sides 50 and 200 (m) plus the maximal area 10000 (m^2) = 10250. Flag as medium since 'sum' composition across mixed units (length + area) is a judgment call. [verified: ok: Width at height x is 400-4x, P=x(400-4x), max x=50: 50 x 200, P=10000 (key). Sum 10250. Stored summary lacks the sum hint.]
